9	/-!
10	# THE FOURTH ANTECEDENT: the chart-finiteness certificate of the real atlas
11	
12	## Why this file exists
13	
14	The board, and every lane working the Picard seam, prices the distance to representability as
15	the three undischarged antecedents of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
16	(`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`): `IsChartUniv`, Zariski-local surjectivity of `Sigma.desc f`,
17	and a representation `rep` of the divisor functor.
18	
19	**That is the antecedent list of the implication, not of the goal.**  The frozen north star of
20	`Challenge.lean` is `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J` with `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`,
21	and `JacobianData` (`Picard/JacobianData.lean`) has **four** fields — `J`, `rep`,
22	`locallyOfFiniteType`, `quasiCompact`.  Accordingly *every* producer of the datum from an atlas
23	takes a fourth input on top of `hf` and the local-surjectivity instance:
24	
25	  `hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)`
26	
27	`JacobianData.ofCharts`, `JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace`,
28	`JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage` and `JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelLifts` all carry it.  So a
29	session that discharged all three tracked antecedents would still not have produced a
30	`JacobianData C`, and nothing in the tree produces `hlft` at any atlas: the only declaration in
31	`Picard/` whose conclusion is `LocallyOfFiniteType` is `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom`, which
32	*takes* `hlft` as a hypothesis.
33	
34	## What is actually owed, and it is much less than the gap suggests
35	
36	`Picard/Pic0ChartPair.lean` states, in prose, that the certificate is "inherited by every
37	restriction: being locally of finite type is local on the source, and an open immersion is
38	locally of finite type".  That sentence is correct and had never been proved — the shape this
39	workspace has repeatedly found to be the least-audited kind of claim.  Discharged here, and the
40	two ingredients are cheap:
41	
42	* `chartHom_restrictChart` (`Pic0ChartPair.lean`) and `chartHom_abelSigmaChart`
43	  (`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean`) identify the structure morphism of a *restricted Abel chart* as
44	  `V.ι ≫ D.hom`;
45	* mathlib's composition instance for `LocallyOfFiniteType` closes the rest, with an open
46	  immersion on the left — `inferInstance` alone, no lemma.
47	
48	So the fourth antecedent, at the **real** atlas (heterogeneous parameters, restricted charts —
49	`mixedParamChart`, `Picard/Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean`), reduces to
50	`LocallyOfFiniteType (D i).hom`: a property of the divisor scheme with no Picard content, no
51	chart parameter, and no dependence on the open `V i`.
52	
53	## Main declarations
54	
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom_mixedParamChart` — the structure morphism of the `i`-th chart of
56	  the mixed-parameter atlas is `(V i).ι ≫ (D i).hom`.
57	* `AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFiniteType_chartHom_mixedParamChart` — **the fourth antecedent
58	  discharged** for the real atlas, from `LocallyOfFiniteType (D i).hom` alone.
59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom_mixedParamChart` — hence the glued object is
60	  locally of finite type over the base field, which is the `JacobianData` field itself.
61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.jacobianDataOfMixedParamCharts` — **the assembly**: the mixed-parameter
62	  atlas plus `hf`, local surjectivity, per-index `LocallyOfFiniteType (D i).hom` and
63	  quasi-compactness of the glued object produce `JacobianData C`.  Landed so that the obligations
64	  that remain are visible in **one signature** rather than spread over four files: everything in
65	  it other than `hf`, the local-surjectivity instance and `rep` is now discharged.
66	
67	## What this does NOT do, stated plainly
68	
69	It closes no gate of the seam.  `IsChartUniv` (`hf`), Zariski-local surjectivity and `rep` are
70	untouched and remain unproduced, and each is another lane's target.  The `quasiCompact` field is
71	*not* discharged here either: for the class-indexed atlas it is genuinely a-posteriori
72	(`JacobianDataCharts.lean` records that `CompactSpace` of the glued object is a theorem about the

74	removed is a *fourth* undischarged antecedent that no row tracked, so that discharging the three
75	tracked ones now genuinely reaches the north star's datum.
76	-/

description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Do not wait for the whole task to be complete. A checkpoint commit must build
  or otherwise be internally coherent, but it may explicitly leave the next
  named obligation open.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

1	/-

     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0Functor
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# The Jacobian representability datum (Wave-4 seam D1, `JacobianData`)
    10	
    11	The pinned representability datum for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative Picard
    12	functor `pic0Functor C` of the challenge curve: a representing object `J`, an honest
    13	`Functor.RepresentableBy` datum (no `Nonempty`, no choice), and the two construction
    14	certificates (`LocallyOfFiniteType`, `QuasiCompact`).  This is the frozen Wave-4
    15	interface shape (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md` §1.1, verbatim), together with the
    16	design-§5 consumers `grpObj` / `homEquiv` / `uniqueUpToIso` — and nothing else.
    17	
    18	## Ownership split (binding, w5-worksheet D1)
    19	
    20	* The **producer** `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, the quasi-compactness certificate,
    21	  and the discharge of the frozen `Jacobian`/`instGrpObj` sorries of `Challenge.lean`
    22	  are **DAT-J property** (the parallel Wave-4 fleet).  None of them lives here.
    23	* This file is the **Wave-5/6/7 consumption interface**: downstream files take
    24	  `(d : JacobianData C)` as a section variable, activate the group structure per proof
    25	  via `letI := d.grpObj` (or `attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`), and
    26	  phrase every statement about `d.J`.  At DAT-J discharge time the frozen gate
    27	  instantiates them by `exact theorem_x … (jacobianData C)` — definitionally, since
    28	  `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`.
    29	* Extensions to this file are **additive only**; the structure shape never changes.
    30	
    31	## The `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage
    32	
    33	`rep` is typed against `(pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat`
    34	so that mathlib's `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies **verbatim** with
    35	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat`.  The functor value at a test `T` is
    36	*definitionally* the coerced subgroup `↥(pic0Subgroup C T)`; `homEquiv` and
    37	`homEquiv_comp` below own this defeq once, exposing the equivalence against
    38	`pic0Subgroup C T` and the naturality against `pic0Map` — no consumer ever meets the
    39	`forget₂ ⋙ forget` spelling again.
    40	
    41	## η-defeq verdict (recon §5 "lower-order unknown", RECORDED)
    42	
    43	**POSITIVE, with one keying caveat.**  `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally equal to
    44	`d.J` (structure-eta for `Comma`/`CostructuredArrow` plus unit-like eta for the
    45	`Discrete PUnit` right leg): the ascription
    46	`(d.grpObj : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom))` elaborates as-is, so **no transport lemma is
    47	ever needed**.  Caveat: bare instance *search* does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own,
    48	so a consumer of `smooth_of_grpObj` — whose group hypothesis is `[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]`
    49	at `f := d.J.hom` — must key the instance at the `Over.mk` spelling:
    50	`letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj` (pure defeq, zero cost; mathlib itself
    51	uses the same ascription idiom in `Group/Smooth.lean`).  Instances stated directly on
    52	`G : Over (Spec (.of K))` (e.g. `IsClosedImmersion η[G].left`) fire on `d.J` with no
    53	massage at all.  The `example`-level smoke tests at the bottom of this file are the
    54	machine-checked record; the T-chain (tangent lane) and S2 (`Smooth` via
    55	`smooth_of_grpObj`) may rely on this freely.
    56	
    57	## Main declarations
    58	
    59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData C` — the frozen datum structure.
    60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.grpObj` — the group-object structure on `d.J` via
    61	  `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` (the discharge route of the frozen `instGrpObj`).
    62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.homEquiv` / `homEquiv_comp` — the universal property
    63	  in consumer form: `(T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T`, natural against `pic0Map`.
    64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.uniqueUpToIso` / `homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom` — any
    65	  two data have canonically isomorphic representing objects (Wave-7's `baseChangeIso`
    66	  mechanism), with the intertwining property.
    67	-/
    68	
    69	set_option autoImplicit false
    70	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    71	
    72	universe u
    73	
    74	open CategoryTheory Opposite
    75	
    76	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    77	
    78	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
    79	
    80	/-- **The pinned representability datum** for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative
    81	Picard functor of the curve `C` (w4-datum-worksheet §1.1, frozen).  Produced once, by
    82	explicit construction, in Wave 4 (DAT-J: `jacobianData`); consumed as a section
    83	variable everywhere else.  NEVER a sorried instance, NEVER `Nonempty` + choice.
    84	
    85	The typing of `rep` is chosen so that `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies verbatim with
    86	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` (see `JacobianData.grpObj`). -/
    87	structure JacobianData (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    88	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    89	    Type (u + 1) where
    90	  /-- The representing object (the Jacobian-to-be). -/
    91	  J : Over (Spec (.of k))
    92	  /-- The pinned universal datum: `Hom(T, J) ≃ Pic⁰(T)`, naturally in the test `T`. -/
    93	  rep : ((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J
    94	  /-- Certificate from the construction (Kleiman 4.8(1) shape); NOT re-derived via the
    95	  EGA limit criterion. -/
    96	  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom
    97	  /-- Certificate from the construction (a posteriori: `|J|` is the image of a
    98	  quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map).  Feeds `IsProper` (Wave 5) via
    99	  `finite type = qc + lft`. -/
   100	  quasiCompact : QuasiCompact J.hom
   101	
   102	namespace JacobianData
   103	
   104	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   105	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   106	
   107	/-- The group-object structure on the representing object, via mathlib's
   108	`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` — this is the (definitional) discharge route of the frozen
   109	`Jacobian.instGrpObj`.  Not a global instance here (the datum is a section variable);
   110	activate per proof with `letI := d.grpObj` or
   111	`attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`. -/
   112	@[implicit_reducible]
   113	noncomputable def grpObj (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj d.J :=
   114	  GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy d.J (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) d.rep
   115	
   116	/-- **The universal property, consumer form**: morphisms into `d.J` are degree-zero
   117	étale Picard classes.  This accessor owns the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq massage once:
   118	the target is the honest subgroup carrier `pic0Subgroup C T`. -/
   119	def homEquiv (d : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} :
   120	    (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T :=
   121	  d.rep.homEquiv
   122	
   123	/-- Naturality of `homEquiv` against the degree-zero restriction maps `pic0Map`
   124	(element form of the `RepresentableBy` naturality, with the functor value unfolded
   125	through `forget₂ ⋙ forget`). -/
   126	theorem homEquiv_comp (d : JacobianData C) {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   127	    (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ d.J) :
   128	    d.homEquiv (f ≫ g) = pic0Map C f (d.homEquiv g) :=
   129	  d.rep.homEquiv_comp f g
   130	
   131	/-- Representing objects are unique up to isomorphism (mathlib
   132	`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso`): any two Jacobian data for the same curve have
   133	canonically isomorphic `J`.  This is Wave-7's `baseChangeIso` mechanism. -/
   134	noncomputable def uniqueUpToIso (d d' : JacobianData C) : d.J ≅ d'.J :=
   135	  d.rep.uniqueUpToIso d'.rep
   136	
   137	/-- The intertwining property of `uniqueUpToIso`: composing with the canonical
   138	isomorphism commutes with the two universal properties. -/
   139	theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom (d d' : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   140	    (f : T ⟶ d.J) :
   141	    d'.homEquiv (f ≫ (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom) = d.homEquiv f := by
   142	  have h : (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom = d'.rep.homEquiv.symm (d.rep.homEquiv (𝟙 d.J)) := rfl
   143	  rw [homEquiv, homEquiv, h, Functor.RepresentableBy.comp_homEquiv_symm]
   144	  exact (d'.rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply _).trans (d.rep.homEquiv_eq f).symm
   145	
   146	end JacobianData
   147	
   148	/-! ## η-defeq smoke tests (recon §5 lower-order unknown; `example`-level, nothing
   149	registered)
   150	
   151	The first test records that `Over.mk d.J.hom ≡ d.J` definitionally (structure eta); the
   152	second that instance resolution crosses it — `smooth_of_grpObj`'s hypothesis
   153	`[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]` at `f := d.J.hom` is discharged by `letI := d.grpObj`; the third
   154	that mathlib's `IsClosedImmersion η[d.J].left` instance fires on `d.J` as-is.  T-chain
   155	and S2 depend on these; if a mathlib bump ever breaks them, a transport lemma must be
   156	added HERE, not in the consumers. -/
   157	
   158	section EtaDefeqSmokeTests
   159	
   160	open MonObj
   161	
   162	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   163	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   164	
   165	/-- Smoke test 1: `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally `d.J` — the ascription
   166	elaborates with no transport. -/
   167	noncomputable example (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj
   168	
   169	/-- Smoke test 2: `smooth_of_grpObj` applies to `d.J.hom` with no transport lemma;
   170	the group instance must be *keyed* at `Over.mk d.J.hom` (the ascribed `letI` below —
   171	instance search does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own, but the ascription is pure
   172	defeq). -/
   173	example (d : JacobianData C) [GeometricallyReduced d.J.hom] : Smooth d.J.hom :=
   174	  letI := d.locallyOfFiniteType
   175	  letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj
   176	  smooth_of_grpObj d.J.hom
   177	
   178	/-- Smoke test 3: the unit section of `d.J` is a closed immersion (mathlib's
   179	group-scheme instance fires on `d.J` directly, with the datum's group structure in
   180	scope). -/
   181	example (d : JacobianData C) [GrpObj d.J] : IsClosedImmersion η[d.J].left :=
   182	  inferInstance
   183	
   184	end EtaDefeqSmokeTests
   185	
   186	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-
     2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors. All rights reserved.
     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
     5	-/
     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.JacobianData
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0SigmaSheaf
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Producing the Jacobian representability datum from a Zariski chart family
    11	
    12	The pinned datum `JacobianData C` of the curve `C` bundles a representing object for the
    13	degree-zero Picard functor together with the two finiteness certificates of that object.
    14	This file constructs it: first from a bare representation (`JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy`),
    15	and then — the substance — from a Zariski chart family of the Σ-extension sheaf, whose glued
    16	scheme is the representing object and whose charts carry the finiteness.
    17	
    18	## Main declarations
    19	
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy` — a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C`
    21	  by `J`, plus `LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom` and `QuasiCompact J.hom`, is a `JacobianData C`.
    22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedHom` / `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedOfCharts` — the glued scheme of a chart
    23	  family, placed over the base field by the Σ-component of the universal element of the
    24	  representation it induces.
    25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom` — the structure morphism `X i ⟶ Spec k` of the `i`-th chart:
    26	  the Σ-component of the element of `pic0SigmaFunctor C` classified by `f i`.
    27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.toGlued_comp_gluedHom` — **the compatibility of the two**: the glue map
    28	  `X i ⟶ gluedOfCharts` composed with the structure morphism of the glued object is exactly
    29	  `chartHom i`.  So the charts are charts *over the base field*, and the glued object is
    30	  covered by them as a `k`-scheme.
    31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` — being locally of finite type is local
    32	  on the source, so it descends from the charts to the glued object.
    33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_gluedHom` — over the affine base `Spec k`, quasi-compactness
    34	  of the glued object is compactness of its space, which a finite family of compact charts
    35	  supplies.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofCharts` — **the first producer of the Jacobian datum**:
    37	  a finite Zariski chart family of relatively representable open immersions into
    38	  `pic0SigmaSheaf C`, jointly locally surjective, with quasi-compact charts that are locally of
    39	  finite type over `k`, yields `JacobianData C`.
    40	
    41	## The hypothesis bundle
    42	
    43	Every declaration here carries exactly the three hypotheses of the frozen `Jacobian` of
    44	`Challenge.lean` — `IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `GeometricallyIrreducible`.  The
    45	`GeometricallyReduced C.hom` hypothesis of `Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` is *not* an extra assumption:
    46	a morphism smooth of relative dimension `1` is smooth (`Smooth.of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one`)
    47	and a smooth morphism is geometrically reduced (`Smooth.geometricallyReduced`), both global
    48	instances of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`, so instance resolution supplies it
    49	from the frozen bundle.  The `example` at the end of this file is the machine-checked record.
    50	-/
    51	
    52	set_option autoImplicit false
    53	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    54	
    55	universe u
    56	
    57	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    58	
    59	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    60	
    61	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    62	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    63	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    64	
    65	/-! ## Packaging a representation as the datum -/
    66	
    67	/-- **Package a representation of the degree-zero Picard functor**, with its two finiteness
    68	certificates, as the pinned Jacobian datum.  The representation is stated in the
    69	`pic0TypeFunctor` spelling; that abbreviation unfolds to the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage that
    70	`JacobianData.rep` is typed against. -/
    71	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    72	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    73	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
    74	    JacobianData C where
    75	  J := J
    76	  rep := rep
    77	  locallyOfFiniteType := hlft
    78	  quasiCompact := hqc
    79	
    80	@[simp]
    81	lemma JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy_J (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    82	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    83	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
    84	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).J = J :=
    85	  rfl
    86	
    87	@[simp]
    88	lemma JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy_rep (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    89	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    90	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
    91	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).rep = rep :=
    92	  rfl
    93	
    94	/-- The universal property of a packaged datum is the packaged representation. -/
    95	@[simp]
    96	lemma JacobianData.homEquiv_ofRepresentableBy (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    97	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    98	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom)
    99	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (g : T ⟶ J) :
   100	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).homEquiv g = rep.homEquiv g :=
   101	  rfl
   102	
   103	/-! ## The chart family and its glued object -/
   104	
   105	section Charts
   106	
   107	variable {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   108	  (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   109	
   110	/-- **The structure morphism of the `i`-th chart** over the base field: the Σ-component of the
   111	element of `pic0SigmaFunctor C` classified by `f i`.  A chart of the degree-zero Picard sheaf
   112	is by construction a scheme *together with* a map to `Spec k`, namely the base over which the
   113	line bundle it classifies lives; this is that map. -/
   114	noncomputable def chartHom (i : ι) : X i ⟶ Spec (.of k) := (yonedaEquiv (f i)).1
   115	
   116	variable (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
   117	variable [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
   118	
   119	/-- **The structure morphism of the glued object of a chart family**: mathlib's 01JJ engine
   120	glues the charts into a scheme representing the Σ-extension sheaf, and the Σ-component of the
   121	universal element of that representation is the map of that scheme to `Spec k`. -/
   122	noncomputable abbrev gluedHom :
   123	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
   124	  ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
   125	    (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1
   126	
   127	/-- **The glued object of a chart family**, as a scheme over the base field.  This is the
   128	object represented by `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`. -/
   129	noncomputable abbrev gluedOfCharts : Over (Spec (.of k)) := Over.mk (gluedHom C f hf)
   130	
   131	/-- The universal element of the glued representation restricts along the `i`-th glue map to
   132	the element classified by `f i`. -/
   133	lemma representableBy_homEquiv_toGlued (i : ι) :
   134	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
   135	      (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i) = yonedaEquiv (f i) :=
   136	  Scheme.LocalRepresentability.yonedaGluedToSheaf_app_toGlued hf
   137	
   138	/-- **The charts are charts over the base field**: the `i`-th glue map into the glued object,
   139	followed by the structure morphism of the glued object, is the structure morphism of the `i`-th
   140	chart.  Both sides are Σ-components of the same restriction of the universal element. -/
   141	lemma toGlued_comp_gluedHom (i : ι) :
   142	    Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i ≫ gluedHom C f hf = chartHom C f i := by
   143	  have h := congrArg Sigma.fst
   144	    ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv_eq
   145	      (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i))
   146	  rw [representableBy_homEquiv_toGlued] at h
   147	  exact h.symm
   148	
   149	/-! ## The two finiteness certificates from the charts -/
   150	
   151	/-- **Locally of finite type descends from the charts**: the property is local on the source
   152	and the glue maps of the glue data cover the glued object, so if each chart is locally of finite
   153	type over the base field then so is the glued object. -/
   154	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)) :
   155	    LocallyOfFiniteType (gluedHom C f hf) := by
   156	  refine IsZariskiLocalAtSource.of_openCover
   157	    (P := @LocallyOfFiniteType) (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover fun i => ?_
   158	  have h := hlft i
   159	  rwa [← toGlued_comp_gluedHom C f hf i] at h
   160	
   161	/-- **Quasi-compactness descends from a finite family of quasi-compact charts**: the base
   162	`Spec k` is affine, so quasi-compactness of the structure morphism is compactness of the space
   163	of the glued object, and that space is the union of the finitely many compact chart images. -/
   164	theorem quasiCompact_gluedHom [Finite ι] (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
   165	    QuasiCompact (gluedHom C f hf) := by
   166	  haveI : Finite (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.I₀ := ‹Finite ι›
   167	  haveI : ∀ i, CompactSpace ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.X i) := hcpt
   168	  haveI : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued :=
   169	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.compactSpace
   170	  exact HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr ‹_›
   171	
   172	/-! ## The producer -/
   173	
   174	/-- **The first producer of the Jacobian datum**: a Zariski chart family of relatively
   175	representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf of the degree-zero Picard functor,
   176	jointly locally surjective, indexed by a finite type, with quasi-compact charts that are locally
   177	of finite type over the base field, produces the pinned representability datum of the curve.
   178	
   179	The representing object is the glued scheme of the family, placed over `Spec k` by the
   180	Σ-component of the universal element; the two certificates are `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom`
   181	and `quasiCompact_gluedHom`. -/
   182	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofCharts [Finite ι]
   183	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
   184	    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
   185	    JacobianData C :=
   186	  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)
   187	    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)
   188	    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)
   189	    (quasiCompact_gluedHom C f hf hcpt)
   190	
   191	@[simp]
   192	lemma JacobianData.ofCharts_J [Finite ι]
   193	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
   194	    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
   195	    (JacobianData.ofCharts C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=
   196	  rfl
   197	
   198	/-- **The producer for an infinite atlas**: same as `JacobianData.ofCharts`, but the index type
   199	is arbitrary and quasi-compactness of the glued object is supplied directly instead of being
   200	derived from finitely many compact charts.
   201	
   202	This is the form the classical construction needs.  The charts of the degree-zero Picard functor
   203	are indexed by divisor *classes* — one chart per class whose twisted fibre class has an effective
   204	witness — and that index set is not finite; compactness of the glued object is then a genuine
   205	theorem about the Jacobian (it is the union of the images of a *quasi-compact* divisor scheme
   206	under the Abel map), not a consequence of finiteness of the atlas.  Note that the
   207	locally-of-finite-type certificate still descends from the charts with no finiteness hypothesis
   208	whatsoever: `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` never uses `Finite ι`. -/
   209	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace
   210	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
   211	    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :
   212	    JacobianData C :=
   213	  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)
   214	    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)
   215	    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)
   216	    (HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr hcpt)
   217	
   218	@[simp]
   219	lemma JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace_J
   220	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
   221	    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :
   222	    (JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=
   223	  rfl
   224	
   225	end Charts
   226	
   227	/-! ## The hypothesis bundle of the frozen `Jacobian` suffices
   228	
   229	`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` introduces `[GeometricallyReduced C.hom]` before its sheaf and
   230	representability statements, while the frozen `Jacobian` of `Challenge.lean` carries only
   231	`IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and `GeometricallyIrreducible`.  There is no gap:
   232	geometric reducedness is *derived* from smoothness of relative dimension one by the global
   233	instances of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`, which is in the import closure of
   234	`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`.  Hence every declaration above elaborates under the frozen bundle alone,
   235	and the example below records it. -/
   236	
   237	example : GeometricallyReduced C.hom := inferInstance
   238	
   239	/-! ## What remains
   240	
   241	`JacobianData.ofCharts` reduces the frozen `Jacobian` of `Challenge.lean` — that is, the
   242	production of `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, from which `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J` —
   243	to a single geometric statement about the degree-zero Picard sheaf of the curve, namely the
   244	existence of a finite Zariski atlas:
   245	
   246	> there exist a finite index type `ι`, schemes `X : ι → Scheme`, and morphisms of presheaves
   247	> `f i : yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaFunctor C` such that
   248	>
   249	> 1. **(relative representability)** each `f i` is a relatively representable open immersion,
   250	>    `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`;
   251	> 2. **(coverage)** the family is jointly locally surjective for the big Zariski topology,
   252	>    `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)`;
   253	> 3. **(chart finiteness)** each chart is locally of finite type over the base field with
   254	>    respect to its own structure morphism, `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)`, and each
   255	>    chart space is quasi-compact, `CompactSpace (X i)`.
   256	
   257	Nothing else about the Picard functor is needed: the sheaf condition is already discharged
   258	(`pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf`), the gluing is mathlib's (`Scheme.LocalRepresentability`), the
   259	Σ-descent to the slice is already discharged (`Functor.RepresentableBy.overSlice`), and the two
   260	certificates of the glued object are discharged here from (3).
   261	
   262	Conditions (1) and (2) are the geometric input — they are what the divisor-scheme/Abel-map
   263	machinery of the `DivScheme…` and `DivRep…` files exists to produce, one chart being carved out
   264	of a symmetric power of the curve by an effectivity locus.  Condition (3) is a property of those
   265	charts alone and does not interact with the Picard functor at all.
   266	
   267	If the atlas that machinery produces is *not* finitely indexed — and the classical one is not,
   268	its charts being indexed by divisor classes — then `JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace` is the
   269	form to use: `ι` is then arbitrary, condition (3) weakens to `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)`
   270	alone, and the second certificate becomes the single statement `CompactSpace` of the glued
   271	object.  That statement is not a bookkeeping hypothesis but a theorem about the Jacobian — the
   272	underlying space is the image of a quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map — and it is
   273	where the quasi-compactness content of the construction actually lives. -/
   274

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]

variable (π) in
/-- **The witness locus of an untwisted class over an affine base**: the set of points of
`Spec B` at which the fibre of the Čech class `c` admits an effective witness divisor with
vanishing `H¹`.

Stated over *classes*, not over data: a basic-open cocycle datum is a presentation, and the
campaign's consumers index charts by a Picard class.  The ∀-quantifier is harmless because
the predicate is class-intrinsic
(`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq`) and every class is
presented (`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq`) — see
`mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists`.

NOT the co-signed `chartLocus c λ` of `w4-datc` §3.3 / `w4-datb` §1.6: that one lives over a
general test, is indexed by a plus class, and reads the TWISTED fibre class.  See the module
header. -/
def cechWitnessLocus (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) : Set (PrimeSpectrum B) :=
  {q : PrimeSpectrum B | ∀ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
    D.cechPicClass = c → D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField}

theorem mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    q ∈ cechWitnessLocus π c ↔ ∀ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
      D.cechPicClass = c → D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- **Membership is testable at any one presentation**: a datum `D` presenting `c` is a
sound and complete test for membership of the witness locus.  This is the class-intrinsicity
of the witness predicate, `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq`, in the form
the consumers use. -/
theorem mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_of_datum {c : (relCurve C B).CechPic}
    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hD : D.cechPicClass = c) (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    q ∈ cechWitnessLocus π c ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField := by
  refine ⟨fun h => h D hD, fun h D' hD' => ?_⟩
  refine (D'.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq D
    q.asIdeal.ResidueField ?_).mpr h
  exact congrArg (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField))
    (hD'.trans hD.symm)

/-- **The ∀-form and the ∃-form of the witness locus agree**: every class is presented by
some datum, and the witness predicate does not depend on which. -/
theorem mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    q ∈ cechWitnessLocus π c ↔ ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
      D.cechPicClass = c ∧ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField := by
  obtain ⟨D₀, hD₀⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (C := C) (π := π) c
  refine ⟨fun h => ⟨D₀, hD₀, h D₀ hD₀⟩, fun ⟨D, hD, h⟩ => ?_⟩
  exact (mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_of_datum D hD q).mpr h

/-- **The class-indexed witness locus is open**: it is the witness locus of any one
presenting datum, and that is open by
`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing` (the audited,
Noetherian-free openness engine).

This is the first *datum-choice-free* openness statement in the campaign — the engine output
is stated for a chosen `D`, which is not something a locus indexed by a Picard class may
depend on.  It is strictly weaker than the reserved `isOpen_chartLocus` (dat-b row B-4),
which assembles this with the shifted-datum constructor and the descent/étale-image
transports; do not cite it as that. -/
theorem isOpen_cechWitnessLocus (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) : IsOpen (cechWitnessLocus π c) := by
  obtain ⟨D₀, hD₀⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (C := C) (π := π) c
  have hset : cechWitnessLocus π c
      = {q : PrimeSpectrum B |
          ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
            Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
                = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField)

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartPair
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# THE ATLAS IS CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEOUS — each chart may carry its own `n`
    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` establishes that at a chart index legal at parameter
    12	`n` the coverage theorem's threshold is forced to equal `n`, and that at `n = g` the resulting
    13	hypothesis is false.  Both that file and the review it adjudicates (I-0660) then reason about
    14	"the" chart parameter, as though the atlas had one.
    15	
    16	**It does not, and this file proves it.**  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
    17	(`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) takes a family `f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf`
    18	indexed by an arbitrary `ι`, with `X : ι → Scheme` and a *per-index* certificate
    19	`hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`.  Nothing ties the `X i` together, so nothing ties
    20	their chart parameters together either: `mixedParamChart` below builds such a family from a
    21	per-index parameter `nn : ι → ℕ`, a per-index representation of `divFunctor C π (nn i)`, and a
    22	per-index chart index legal *at that index's own parameter*.
    23	
    24	## Why this matters, and it changes the shape of the residue
    25	
    26	The `b = n` calibration is per-chart.  So the question "can coverage use DAT-0a's threshold?"
    27	does not have to be answered uniformly: a point whose splitting field has threshold `b_L` can be
    28	covered by *the chart whose parameter is `b_L.toNat`*, and a different point by a different
    29	chart.  The I-0204 non-uniformity of `m` — no single exponent works for every fibre — is
    30	therefore **not** an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument for an atlas indexed by the
    31	threshold, which is what a heterogeneous family is.
    32	
    33	What this does **not** do, and the honest limit of the observation:
    34	
    35	* it does not produce the representations.  `mixedParamChart` takes `rep i` as a hypothesis, one
    36	  per parameter, and the divisor-representability lane supplies `divFunctor C π g` — a single
    37	  parameter.  So the heterogeneous atlas is *admissible* but not yet *inhabited* beyond `n = g`;
    38	* it does not discharge `IsChartUniv` at any index (still CERT-Σ-gated, `Pic0ChartPair.lean`);
    39	* it says nothing about local surjectivity, which is DAT-B B-6 and is what would actually consume
    40	  the freedom.
    41	
    42	So the correct statement of the residue, refining `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s: **B-5's step 3
    43	is a question about which parameters `divFunctor C π n` is representable at, not about
    44	reconciling one parameter with one threshold.**  If representability is available only at `n = g`
    45	then the slack must go into `Z` (and its legality is open, as recorded there); if it is available
    46	at every `n`, coverage can be assembled chart-by-chart against each fibre's own threshold and the
    47	`b = n` forcing is harmless.  That is a sharper question than either prior reading, and it is
    48	addressed to the divRep lane rather than to this one.
    49	
    50	## Main declarations
    51	
    52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamChart` — a chart family with a per-index chart parameter.
    53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart` — its `hf` clause is exactly a
    54	  per-index `IsChartUniv`, so heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate.
    55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamRepresentableBy` — such a family is admissible input to
    56	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  **This is the whole point**: the DAT-glue seam never sees a
    57	  chart parameter.
    58	-/
    59	
    60	set_option autoImplicit false
    61	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    62	
    63	universe u
    64	
    65	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    66	
    67	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    68
